items.title: CVE-2026-68820: Windows WinSock Zero-Day Exploited in the Wild — Patch Tuesday Aug 2026
items.summary: Microsoft's August 2026 Patch Tuesday fixed 398 CVEs including CVE-2026-68820, a use-after-free flaw in the Windows Ancillary Function Driver for WinSock (afd.sys). A locally authenticated attacker triggers a race condition to escalate privileges to SYSTEM with no user interaction required. Active exploitation confirmed in the wild.
items.why: SYSTEM-level privilege escalation with zero user interaction is a staple post-exploitation move for ransomware groups. One of three zero-days patched in this record-breaking Patch Tuesday; apply immediately.

items.title: CVE-2026-63077: JetBrains TeamCity Unauthenticated RCE (CVSS 9.8) Added to CISA KEV
items.summary: A critical deserialization bug in JetBrains TeamCity On-Premises (all versions before 2025.11.7 / 2026.1.3) lets unauthenticated remote attackers bypass authentication and execute arbitrary OS commands as the TeamCity server process. CISA added it to KEV on August 5 with an unusually tight 3-day remediation deadline.
items.why: CI/CD servers are prime targets — compromise lets attackers poison build pipelines, steal signing keys, and backdoor software before it ships. Unauthenticated and remotely exploitable with CVSS 9.8.

items.title: CVE-2026-18577: N-able N-central Auth Bypass (CVSS 8.2) Exploited to Pivot Into Managed Endpoints
items.summary: An authentication bypass flaw in N-able N-central (pre-2026.3.1.7) lets unauthenticated attackers seize admin accounts remotely. Threat actors then abuse the built-in Take Control feature and deploy Cloudflare Tunnels for persistent, stealthy access to every managed endpoint in the MSP's portfolio. Exploitation confirmed since August 1, 2026.
items.why: One compromised N-central server cascades to thousands of client endpoints across an entire MSP's customer base — a supply-chain-style blast radius. CISA mandated federal remediation by August 6.

items.title: Iranian APT Screening Serpens Deploys 6 New RAT Variants Against US, Israel & UAE Defense Sector
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 tracked Screening Serpens (UNC1549 / Smoke Sandstorm) running aggressive cyber-espionage operations against tech and defense entities in the US, Israel, and UAE from February–April 2026. The group used AppDomainManager hijacking and six newly developed RAT variants delivered via fake job-posting lures, timed to align with the Middle East conflict that erupted February 28.
items.why: The novel AppDomainManager hijacking technique evades many EDR solutions. Unit 42 warns the group shows no signs of slowing — organizations in defense, aerospace, and critical tech should expect continued targeting.

items.title: ~800 Malicious npm Packages Deploy WEL1DROPPER Cross-Platform RAT in Supply Chain Campaign
items.summary: The 'Flooding Dropper' campaign (tracked by Sonatype) flooded npm with ~800 AI-generated typosquatted packages delivering WEL1DROPPER — a cross-platform dropper for Windows, macOS, and Linux. It disables ETW and AMSI, establishes persistence, then pulls further payloads via Cloudflare Workers or DNS TXT records from a Russian-hosted C2 domain (wel1[.]ru).
items.why: AI-generated typosquatting at 800-package scale sets a new bar for npm supply chain attacks. AMSI/ETW bypass combined with multi-OS targeting lets the malware evade standard endpoint defenses across entire developer environments.
